### 2026-10-18 – Hello Everyone! Over the past two days, I've worked on my project, Smooth Run, a super smooth marble run. The following is my journal for both days.

**7h**

Hello Everyone! Over the past two days, I've worked on my project, Smooth Run, a super smooth marble run. The following is my journal for both days.

10/17/26

I came home really late, and got straight to work. I sttarted on the guide and setup onshape. Total:

30 minutes (No photos, but all I really did was set up onshape.

10/18/26

Time to pull an all day project development. To begin with, I started with the guide to do the straight line marble track as well as the base. For the base, I really just drew a random, smooth shape with the 3D spline tool. I also made the sweep profile and path using the guide. Using the plane tool at a point was pretty cool, but soon, it'll make me go insane

Base:
![20261019_003757_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/1e9cc76ab5de8dcc62109e41f3a239c8ae36e2c70d8bcd1ecd12d38bb3707ab5.png)

Sweep Profile:

![20261018_193220_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/17b25cdf33fbb458c03a37b327cb1f7b3d7208caed9b2b221b7c19b7c889a274.png)

Then, I used the sweep tool to make my first track!

![20261018_193324_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/28ac1b3cd1145a66844e274aac2309f0c732cfa059bd1d7ccc2cc9a242783702.png)

After this, I decided that the track would have a slight tilt, go downwards, and curve around. I edited the startup line to have a slight slant. Now comes the majority of the time spent on this track: planes. See, marble runs are sort of like a free form brush in a 3d space. However, onshape sketches take place on 2d planes that can't be moved freely. They must be in relation to a plane, point, or line, with an offset sometimes possible. for my curve downwards, I thought a curve on a flat plane would work, so I used a plane parallel to the top plane using  the point plane relation. However, immediately I realized I was wrong. A curve would need to be at a constant downward tilt. It also
 needs to be tilted slightly left, so gravity can do its thing.

(Originally, I thought I could just use the top plane, but it caused a track disconnection).
![20261018_195019_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/52586bef941427d10c2daf237426ecf64008cff8c005865f22414a100495b936.png)

Then,  I tried two use line angle relation two get a plane that is parallel to the original track (slight downward tilt). I drew a line and then tilted it to the left using another line angle relation. Then I realized another thing: Because  the track turns around, if both halves of the curve were on the same plane, then the curve returning back to the origin would be upwards. To fix this, I only drew 1/2 of the curve on the plane, then created another curve that goes downward on a new plane with an opposite angle.

First try (Completely downward tilt):
![20261018_204451_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/c89d32c0b1b24a6e6907f9bf2465c
3456370a48d7fc4540fd2f8efdb4918a9a2.png)

Second try(Left and downward tilt)

Explanation of plane issue:

![Untitled drawing](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/cf9dfa25110ea66e348d56c1ab283e24eca708ce6717ba70a16dde5e6df1a165.png)

After doing the first part the rest of it became easy. I had a straight plunge down followed by a doodle like marble track with a lot of curves using the spline tool.

![20261019_001113_grim](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/KQCyBcYn6IogPFBuWHZ5GfGedGnxxuWs/c096d59e40447f62dfb78564b5767abb1af9434bad93c35cebf3d00b958306d0.png)

I then did something the guide didn't show: make each part (track, base, funnel, and ball)  a separate part and combine them with an assembly. The ball was easy and I kept everything on the same base as I really wanted a scalable design, with the ball shrinking proportionally to the size of the track when printing.

Funnel Sketch (originally, I put the line 10 milimeters away even though the revoltue would make a 20 millimeter hole, I soon changed it to 5 mm).
